flow.costPlain: Running Snowflake's platform — data centers and the cost of delivering its product and services.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 23% YoY — growing, but slower than revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 33% YoY — the fastest-growing cost line.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 35% YoY.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $138.79 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — while other income added $4.19 and tax cost $0.21, leaving a $34.81 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $942,094K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $58.9M (a 6% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $365.5M, other income covered $39.5M of that and tax cost $1.9M, so the chart draws the remaining $327.9M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source.
oneTimers: A $17.5M restructuring charge for a restructuring plan at a majority-owned subsidiary ($7.7M in cost of revenue, $9.9M in R&D), booked inside operating results and excluded from non-GAAP results.
$1.3M of expenses associated with acquisitions and strategic investments, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
$0.7M of amortization of debt issuance costs on the $2.3B of 0% convertible senior notes issued in September 2024, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $39.5M, net: $48.7M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, less $0.7M of interest expense and $8.5M of other expense, net. Income tax was a $1.9M provision. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $324.3M (EPS -$0.98), after $3.6M of loss attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 29% YoY and 96% of all revenue; product gross profit was $636.7M, a 71% margin.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 17% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (a $15.5M gross loss).

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 29% to $900.3M, the net revenue retention rate was 127%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 55% to $5.7B. Snowflake guided Q4 FY25 product revenue to $906–$911M, up 23%, at a 4% non-GAAP operating margin.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $365.5M, wider than the $260.6M loss a year ago. The main reason: $381.4M of stock-based compensation-related charges, including about $9.3M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $58.9M, a 6% margin (down from 10% a year ago).
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 542 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+25% YoY) and 754 Forbes Global 2000 customers (+8% YoY). Operating cash flow was $101.7M and adjusted free cash flow was $86.8M.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 28% to $942.1M, with product revenue up 29% to $900.3M — but $381.4M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $365.5M and a net loss of $327.9M.
